ORDER (Per Sandesh D. Patil, J.) :
1) By the present Interim Application, the Applicant is seeking several reliefs.

Presently, the following reliefs are pressed for ;
a) That pending the hearing and disposal of the main Family Court Appeal, this Hon'ble Court by an order and injunction be pleased to restrain the Respondent by herself and/or through her family members and/or through her agents and servants from obstructing the Applicant, his mother, wife and children ingress and egress in and out of his own flat at Raj Classic and from disturbing the Applicant and his mother, wife and children use, occupation and possession of the flat at Raj Classic.
b) That pending he hearing and disposal of the main Family Court Appeal, this Hon'ble Court be pleased to pass an order directing the Respondent not to invite and/or allow her relatives and strangers to live in the Applicant's flat at Raj Classic without his permission.
2) It appears that the Applicant had filed Petition No.A- 904. ia 12554-2025.doc 883 of 2016 under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1995 ("the said Act") in the Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai and the Respondent-wife had filed a petition seeking restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the said Act by filing proceeding bearing Petition No.A-597 of 2016, also in the Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai.
3) The proceedings filed by both the parties were clubbed together by an order dated 20/12/2016, as the parties to the proceedings were same.
4) The learned Principal Judge, Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai, passed the following Order and disposed of both the proceedings :-
ORDER:
1. .. No.597/2016 is dismissed.

9. The respondent shall deposit Rs.15,00,000/- in his and his daughter's name jointly in any 904. ia 12554-2025.doc nationalized bank which shall be allowed to be withdrawn along with interest by his daughter only at the time of her marriage or when she turn 30 years of age, whichever is earlier.
10. Decree be drawn up accordingly.

5) It is informed by the learned Advocate for the Applicant that both the parties have filed Family Court Appeals, challenging the judgment and order dated 21/10/2022 in this Court and the same are pending for admission.
6) Learned Counsel appearing for the Applicant submitted that the marriage between the parties which was solemnized on 18/3/1999, was dissolved by a decree of divorce.
Learned Counsel for the Applicant further submits that the Applicant has remarried after the decree of divorce, as, there was no appeal preferred by the Respondent-wife, within the statutory period.
She further states that the Applicant resides in Thailand with his wife and two small children and visits India with his family.

She states that in 2024, the Applicant suffered a stroke and was admitted to the hospital in India/Thailand and that the Applicant had to undergo 904. ia 12554-2025.doc a surgery for placement of stent to treat his brain occlusion.
She states that the Applicant is required to take treatment in India, as the treatment in Thailand is very expensive.
She further states that in April 2024, the Applicant along with his newly wedded wife and two children had come to India, however, they were not allowed to stay in the Applicant's flat.
Learned Counsel for the Applicant states that the Applicant wants to bring his wife and two children permanently to India, and that the family wants to migrate to India.

She states that, hence, the Applicant wants to stay in the flat A/1003/1004, Raj Classic, New Yari Rod, Andheri (West),
Mumbai (hereinafter referred to as the 'said flat'), where the Respondent and Applicant were residing.

7) She further states that on the Applicant's trip to India on 8/4/2024, when he came with his wife and two children, the Respondent created a ruckus and threw away all the food items which were prepared for the Applicant's children.
She further states that now the Applicant has come to India for the Diwali vacation and wants to stay in the said flat with his family.
She 904.
states that on 24/9/2025 when the Applicant went to the said flat, the mother of the Respondent opened the door and used derogatory words and insulted the Applicant.

She states that again when the Applicant went on 26/9/2025, he found that the door was bolted from inside by a safety chain; that when the Applicant tried to enter the house, the Respondent did not permit him to enter the house, as a result of which he had to stay out.

Thus, learned Counsel for the Applicant prays that the Applicant be permitted to stay in the said flat with his family who has Rajesh Ahlawat vs Sharmila Rajesh Ahlawat Nee Sharmila D. ... on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140779111/
4 come with him from Thailand.

sentences.text:
8) Learned Counsel appearing for the Respondent-wife on the other hand stated that the Respondent-wife has no objection if the Applicant and his mother come and reside there, however,
she has an objection to the Applicant's wife and children coming to the said flat.
Learned Counsel for the Respondent states the Respondent has never stopped the Applicant/his mother from visiting the said flat.
He states that there are about four rooms in the said flat, one, which is the master bedroom, which is occupied 904.
by the Applicant and that the Respondent is using another bedroom and her daughter is using yet another bedroom
. He states that one bedroom is not occupied by any one.
9) The learned Counsel for the Respondent stated that if if the Applicant is allowed to bring his wife and children out of the new marriage, it will definitely cause much trauma and concern to her.
Learned Counsel for the Respondent, therefore, prayed that the appropriate orders may be passed as against the Applicant and his mother.
However, the Respondent staunchly objects newly wedded wife of the Applicant and their children to come and stay in the said flat.

The learned Counsel appearing for the Respondent further informs that the Applicant has got another house which is in the name of mother of the Applicant and that the Applicant can very well stay over there.
He further informs that the present application is filed merely to harass the Respondent.
10) We have heard the learned Counsel appearing for the 904. ia 12554-2025.doc respective parties.
We have perused the copy of the Interim Application No.12554 of 2025.
The Respondent wife has no objection if the Applicant and his old mother come and stay in the said flat.
She, however, has got an objection for the newly wedded wife of the Applicant and the children out of the new wedlock to come and reside in the said flat.
As per the contention of the Applicant himself, when, last time the Applicant had gone to stay in the said flat along with his wife and children, the Respondent had created ruckus.
It is the case of Applicant that the Respondent wife had thrown away the food which was prepared for the children of the Applicant.
We are of the considered opinion that if the newly wedded wife of the Applicant and their children are allowed to stay in the said flat, there would be further disharmony between the parties.
11) In this premises, we deem it fit that permission is granted only to the Applicant and his mother to stay in the said flat.

The learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Mumbai, had in its order dated 21/10/2022 ordered that the said flat should be 904. ia 12554-2025.doc equally divided amongst the parties into equal portion.

Both the parties are,
however, not agreeable with the judgment and order dated 21/10/2022 and have preferred Family Court Appeals in this Court.
It will take some time to decide the Family Court Appeals on merits.
The Family Court Appeal Nos.27 of 2024, 26 of 2024 and 20 of 2023 and the Interim Application Nos.4110 of 2023 and 13099 of 2023 in FCA No.20 of 2023 are also pending.
